TcLOVValue.description: Almost Impossible (No controls exist. Issue likely to escape to customer or field before detection)
Very Remote (Existing controls unlikely to identify the issue. Detection would rely on chance)
Remote (Detection possible but inconsistent; issue likely to escape)
Low (Detection dependent on operator awareness or manual review)
Marginal (Existing controls provide some opportunity to detect the issue)
Moderate (Standard inspection or process checks likely to find the issue)
Good (Multiple checks exist with a high chance of detection)
Very Good (Automated or structured controls usually identify the issue before release)
High (Robust prevention and detection mechanisms in place)
Almost Certain (Error-proofed process (poka-yoke), automated detection, or issue physically cannot escape)
Component change
Packaging, shipping
Part non-conformity
Vehicle-level or cross-functional issues requiring alignment across vehicle systems (e.g. Body to Powertrain)
Incompatibilities between different Areas of Competence within the same function (e.g. Body Engineering: Exterior Mechanisms to Body-in-White) Escalation: Functional Head
Incompatibilities between teams within the same Area of Competence (e.g. Exterior Trim: Exterior Mechanisms to Exterior Trim). Escalation: Head of Area
Incompatibilities within the same SET that can be resolved locally (e.g. Exterior Mechanisms to Exterior Mechanisms). Escalation: SET Leader

001 < Risk Score < 399
Almost Certain (Expected to occur on every build or deployment without mitigation)
Extremely High (Very likely to occur; known issue with repeated history)
High (Likely to occur on multiple vehicles/processes)
Moderately High (Has occurred before; credible risk without robust controls)
Moderate (Could reasonably occur under normal operating conditions)
Occasional (Known possibility but not expected frequently)
Low (Unlikely but plausible)
Very Low (Rare occurrence; limited historical evidence)
Remote (Highly unlikely; strong controls in place)
Almost Impossible (No known mechanism for occurrence)
Safety issue, legislative non-compliance, stop-build condition, vehicle grounding, campaign risk (= A1)
Vehicle/component inoperable, loss of primary function, major warranty exposure (= A2)
Severe performance degradation requiring immediate containment (= A2 / B1)
Significant customer-impacting performance issue, major production disruption (= B1)
Noticeable customer concern, significant process impact, moderate warranty risk (= B1)
Moderate quality concern requiring additional manufacturing effort (= B2)
Customer perceptible fit & finish issue, minor warranty impact (= B2)
Low customer impact, manageable process concern (= B2 / C)
Internal process, BOM or efficiency issue with no customer impact (= C)
Administrative change, BOM tidy-up, cost reduction, continuous improvement (= C)
